migrationImportStep.startFailed: The import could not be started.
migrationImportStep.suppressionStartFailed: The suppression import could not be started.
migrationImportStep.flagsOff: Both integration imports are switched off for this workspace. Turn on {mailchimpFlag} and {mandrillFlag} under {settingsLink} to carry your history across.
migrationImportStep.explainer: Contacts and their Mailchimp unsubscribes import first; Mandrill's reject list follows on its own. Only one import runs at a time, so the second starts when the first finishes. Running this again later is safe — every address is matched on its email, so nothing is duplicated.
migrationImportStep.nothingToCarry: Nothing new to carry — the suppression list here already matches.

migrationPresetStep.bulletStreams: {streams} all move to the measured split ({strategy}) over your own MTA and Mailchimp Transactional.
migrationPresetStep.bulletFallback: Mailchimp Transactional becomes the deliverability-fallback relay for each of them.
migrationPresetStep.bulletPace: Every stream ramps at the {pace} pace — smaller steps, more clean windows per step. You can change it later on the ramp controls screen.
migrationPresetStep.bulletStart: Your own MTA starts at {share} of traffic. Nothing about today's delivery changes; Owlat starts measuring both arms on identical instrumentation.
migrationPresetStep.stoppedAt: Stopped at the {write}. Everything listed above is already in place — fix the problem above and apply again; re-applying what landed is harmless.

mtaStsModeCard.title: Inbound TLS policy (MTA-STS)
mtaStsModeCard.subtitle: Let senders require encrypted delivery to your mail server

descriptions.none: No policy is published. Senders deliver mail to you exactly as they do today.
descriptions.testing: A policy is published, but senders only report TLS problems — they never fail delivery. The safe first step while you watch for issues.
descriptions.enforce: Senders must deliver over verified TLS or the message is rejected. Turn this on only once testing looks clean.

savedToasts.none: MTA-STS turned off — no policy is published.
savedToasts.testing: MTA-STS set to testing — senders will report TLS problems without failing delivery.
savedToasts.enforce: MTA-STS set to enforce — publish the DNS records so senders require verified TLS.

mtaStsModeCard.dnsRecords: Add the {policyRecord} and {hostRecord} DNS records on the {domainsLink} so senders can find and trust this policy.
mtaStsModeCard.enforceWithoutHost: No inbound mail host is configured, so an enforced policy can't be served yet. Set up receiving first, or switch back to testing.
mtaStsModeCard.adminsOnly: Only owners and admins can change this.

postmasterComplianceCard.title: Gmail compliance
postmasterComplianceCard.subtitle: What Google Postmaster Tools reports about your sending domains
postmasterComplianceCard.unavailableBody: Google’s view of your sending could not be read just now, so this card is showing nothing rather than guessing. Your mail is unaffected — this card only reads.
postmasterComplianceCard.notConnectedBody: Sending works exactly the same without this. Connecting a free Google Postmaster account adds Gmail's own view of your spam rate and authentication, which raises measurement confidence.
postmasterComplianceCard.allClear: Google reports no failing checks for your sending domain. | Google reports no failing checks for your sending domains.
